Today 14 stocks pass all five rules: LULU, ACGL, GL, HIG, DECK, UHS, CB, CMCSA, GOOG, GOOGL, TRV, LDOS, BKNG and EME. 17 more miss by one rule: SYF, NFLX, PTC, NVDA, PGR, AIZ, TPR, RJF, MSCI, FIX, LII, AXP, RMD, AOS, INTU, FFIV and META.

Backtest: the 11 picks of 16 Nov 2021 are up +90% (+13.7% a year) price only, against +71% for every stock screened and +58% for the S&P 500 (price only). Details below.

How the values are worked out

How it works. Official figures from each company's SEC filings (Yahoo for the few foreign filers): the last twelve months' net income ÷ shares, plus net cash. Value with no growth = EPS × 13.1 + net cash; growth needed = the yearly growth for 5 years (15x exit, 10% return) that makes the value equal the price. Green ≤ 5% a year, blue 5–25%, red ≥ 25% or no earnings. Financials use book value × 5-year ROE (no net cash), energy and materials average the 12-month and 5-year EPS and are capped at blue, real estate is not valued, and cash conversion below 70% caps at blue. Lenders: book value less nonaccrual loans the allowance doesn't cover; nonaccrual loans above 2% of loans, an allowance below them, or net charge-offs (NCO) up by half on a year earlier cap at blue. Grade = profit growth vs price growth over about 3 years (A = P/E fell 25%+ … D = rose a third+). A filter, not a verdict.

Screen – 14 shortlisted, 17 near misses of 488

The five rules

  1. Cheap. The P/E is 18 or less (the price less net cash, divided by the earnings per share the valuation uses).
  2. Growing. Earnings per share grew at least 15% a year over both the last 5 years and the last 3.
  3. Profitable every year. No loss year in that window.
  4. Worth holding. At least 10% a year expected over a 5-year hold, if growth slows to half its past rate (at most 15%) and the shares are sold at 15x earnings. Dividends are not counted.
  5. Clean books. At least 70% of profit arrives as cash, no demerger or one-off history, no bad-loan warning, and up-to-date results.

Near miss = one rule short: a P/E up to 22 with growth met, growth down to 12% with the P/E met, or only the return short. Insider ownership is shown (US companies have no promoter group), not flagged. EPS from SEC filings, diluted and put on today's share basis. The shortlist, the near misses and every green signal have a page with the working and up to 20 years of prices.

Change the rules

Of 488 companies, 283 have clean books and a profit every year, 66 of those grew fast enough, 18 of those are cheap enough, and 14 of those promise enough return – the shortlist.

    Survivorship bias: today's members are the ones that did well enough to be in the index now, so every average here – picks and all screened alike – flatters; compare the picks with all screened rather than with the index. Past performance only, and a handful of picks is a small sample.

    How the backtest was done

    How it was done. On each date: today's members (the index then is not in the data), each rebuilt exactly as filed by that day – only the SEC figures filed on or before it (later restatements ignored), the share count then, and the price then on the share basis of then (splits both ways) – and the same rules as the screen above: P/E ≤ 18, EPS growth ≥ 15% over 5 and 3 years, every year profitable, ≥ 10% expected over the hold. Foreign filers are left out (their figures are today's). Returns to today: the picks equal-weighted, price only on both sides – the stored US prices carry no dividends (about 1.5% a year for the S&P 500).
